old_problem: The historical review correctly recognized the danger of inventing an SDR but treated the entire operation as undefined and also required a generic SDR checksum that the IPMI record format does not contain. IPMI 2.0 sections 33.1-33.14, section 43 and Appendix G define the repository modes, complete-record Add request, returned Record ID, record header/key/body model, length rule, Get SDR readback and Delete SDR recovery primitive. The exact disposable record bytes and platform effect remain Project artifacts that can be safely parameterized rather than retaining Pending.
disposition_reason: On a writable repository with authoritative Add 24h and targeted Delete 26h support, add exactly one owner-approved, absent, inert disposable SDR whose complete 5+Record-Length bytes fit one local request. Respect the advertised modal/non-modal update mode; 24h carries only the complete SDR bytes and no reservation. Require completion 00h plus a non-selector assigned Record ID, acquire a fresh reservation because Add may cancel the old one, reconstruct the stored record with bounded 23h reads, compare its assigned-ID header and every remaining byte, prove the expected monitoring footprint and no unintended sensor/control behavior, then reserve again and delete that exact key/ID once. Reconcile the repository by record-key/body multiset because Record IDs and timestamps may legitimately change. Never guess standard/OEM fields, use full clear, substitute Partial Add, retry an ambiguous Add or claim that a raw repository hash must remain identical.
decision_basis: Master XLSX rows 1081-1086, exact same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT second review, tests_gpt_merged, selection manifest and historical V3.1 record were directly read. tests.json contains one occurrence of this code. The related OOB Add SDR is row 1211 / variant 46f47bb0079c403e and remains separate. Formal queue sequence 75 was independently verified as row 1085 / variant ad220be16ce32a7f.

IPMI v2.0 Appendix G assigns Add SDR to Storage NetFn 0Ah/Cmd 24h. Section 33.13 requires the complete SDR data in one request and returns completion plus a two-byte Record ID, least-significant byte first. No reservation fields precede the 24h payload.

Section 43 defines every SDR as a five-byte header followed by contiguous record-key fields and a type-specific body. Header bytes are Record ID (two), SDR Version, Record Type and Record Length; Record Length is the number of bytes after that field, so the complete vector length must equal 5+Record-Length.

There is no generic checksum field in the standard SDR record model. Transport message checksums are handled by the IPMI interface, while only an authoritative OEM schema may define checks inside OEM data. The prior blanket checksum requirement is therefore corrected, not guessed.

Record IDs are repository access handles, can be recycled or reassigned after add/delete and must not be assumed sequential. The two-byte ID returned by 24h is authoritative; subsequent retrieval must also match the record's stable key fields and body.

Section 33.2 distinguishes non-modal repositories, writable without disrupting other commands, from modal repositories that require Enter/Exit SDR Repository Update Mode and may reject most other commands with D0h. The Project must bind the advertised/authoritative mode before mutation; unspecified mode is NOT READY rather than a license to probe both paths.

Get SDR Repository Info provides record count, free space, add/erase timestamps, overflow and update-mode/delete/partial/reservation capability bits. Capacity must cover the complete record and allocation behavior before 24h; a full record that exceeds the local transport request limit belongs to the distinct Partial Add testcase and cannot be cross-credited.

Add can cancel an existing reservation. Full reconstruction via Get SDR 23h at nonzero offsets requires a current reservation, so readback and later Delete must use fresh reservations and must stop on cancellation rather than retry automatically.

SDRs describe expected sensors, devices, thresholds and initialization behavior; an invalid record can create false topology or control decisions. A safe generic Add validation therefore needs an owner-approved inert disposable record and an explicit no-unexpected-monitoring oracle, not an invented sensor record or duplicate.

Targeted Delete SDR 26h is optional but is the bounded recovery for this parameterized test. If exact delete is unavailable and the record is not an intentional approved permanent configuration change with independent recovery, execution is NOT READY; Clear SDR Repository is explicitly prohibited.

ED-02 preserves the distinct Source Key/variant; ED-03 separates standard framing from OEM payload authority; ED-13/ED-15 govern N/A and acceptance; ED-17 protects evidence; ED-19 separates IB/OOB; ED-28/ED-30 require recovery; ED-34 parameterizes the record; ED-38 prohibits automatic retry.

test_case.test_name: IPMI Add SDR (IB Storage 0Ah/24h) complete approved record, assigned-ID readback and targeted removal
test_case.purpose: Exercise the in-band complete-record Add SDR command with one absent, owner-approved disposable record, verify its repository-assigned identity, exact stored bytes and bounded monitoring effect, then remove only that record and reconcile the original logical repository without clearing it or substituting Partial Add/OOB coverage.
required_package: Approved BMC/firmware/local interface with a writable SDR repository, authoritative Add 24h and Delete 26h support, and a versioned raw runner that can carry the complete record in one request

Version-controlled APPROVED_SDR_BYTES and decoded schema: repository-approved Record-ID placeholder, 51h or otherwise authoritative version, record type, Record-Length satisfying total=5+length, unique key fields, complete body, and—if OEM—registered IANA plus owner-defined data with no guessed bytes

Proof the record is inert/disposable or an exact approved effect oracle; duplicate/key-collision scan; immutable raw baseline export; canonical baseline keyed by record type/key/body; repository/consumer/alert inventory
Get SDR Repository Info and optional allocation results proving update mode, no overflow and adequate allocation; verified request-size limit proving the complete 24h payload fits without using 25h

Fresh-reservation/chunked Get SDR reader, exact returned-ID parser, targeted Delete 26h recovery, modal Exit path if applicable, maintenance window, explicit confirmation and independent BMC/monitoring owner
test_case.test_command: AUTHORIZED SDR MUTATION PROCEDURE; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Record Source Key/variant and target; export every SDR raw and decoded, capture 0Ah/20h info/allocation/mode, build a canonical multiset excluding volatile Record IDs, and prove APPROVED_SDR_BYTES' key is absent. Validate every byte against its standard or owner OEM schema, total length=5+header length, approved Record-ID placeholder, uniqueness, inert/effect oracle, adequate capacity and one-request transport fit; do not invent a record checksum. Require Delete 26h recovery and no incident hold. For modal mode, enter 0Ah/2Ah once and pre-authorize 2Bh exit recovery; for non-modal, do not enter update mode. Display the entire redacted/hashed record and recovery for immediate approval, then send once over `-I open`: Storage 0Ah/24h followed directly by all APPROVED_SDR_BYTES, with no reservation prefix. Require completion 00h and exactly one assigned ID RID that is neither 0000h nor FFFFh. Do not repeat an ambiguous Add; enumerate by unique key instead. Acquire a fresh 0Ah/22h reservation because Add may cancel reservations, then reconstruct RID via bounded 0Ah/23h chunks from offset 0 and compare header RID plus every byte 3..N to the fixture. Exit modal mode once if entered, prove the approved monitoring/alert effect and absence of unintended sensors/controls, then acquire another fresh reservation, re-read RID header/key, and issue 0Ah/26h only for that exact RID. Require delete completion/returned RID, prove the key absent, reconcile record count/free-space/overflow and the original canonical key/body multiset, and document legitimate ID/timestamp changes. Never use 25h, 27h clear, initialization agent, reset or OOB Add as a substitute.
test_case.expected_result: The complete one-request 24h Add returns completion 00h and one valid assigned RID. Fresh-reservation 23h reads reconstruct exactly one stored record whose header contains RID and whose version/type/length/key/body match the approved fixture byte-for-byte; repository count/add timestamp and capacity change coherently, and only the approved monitoring footprint appears. Targeted 26h deletion returns the same RID, the unique key disappears, overflow remains clear, repository count returns to baseline, and the canonical type/key/body multiset and monitoring state match baseline even if access IDs and add/erase timestamps changed. Unsupported/read-only/Add-absent is N/A only with authoritative platform evidence. Any ambiguity, duplicate, mismatch, unintended effect or incomplete recovery is FAIL/NOT READY without retry.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact IB identity, authoritative writable/Add/Delete capability, a complete one-request approved record with valid header/length and unique key, capacity/mode/transport proof, immediate approval, one 24h completion plus valid RID, complete chunked 23h byte equality, expected monitoring behavior, exact-key 26h removal and canonical repository recovery. FAIL covers guessed standard/OEM fields, invented checksum assumptions, header-length mismatch, invalid/ambiguous RID, duplicate/key collision, partial/normalized body mismatch, unexpected sensor/threshold/control/alert behavior, use of Partial Add or OOB evidence, clear/reset, automatic retry or failed deletion/reconciliation. NOT READY covers missing fixture, schema, capacity, mode, request fit, Delete/recovery, containment or approval. N/A requires authoritative read-only or Add-unsupported evidence; a single command error is insufficient.
safety_gate: Use one owner-approved disposable record whose stable key is absent and whose monitoring/control effect is explicitly bounded. Do not create a plausible generic sensor, duplicate an existing key or guess OEM IANA/data.
Preserve the full repository and downstream monitoring state before mutation. Do not clear SDR, SEL or OS logs; Clear SDR Repository 27h is never recovery for this case.
Require the complete record to fit one 24h request. If it does not, mark this Add path NOT READY/N/A as governed by the platform and review Partial Add separately; never cross-credit 25h.
Honor exactly one authoritative modal/non-modal path. In modal mode, retain independent access and a preapproved Exit 2Bh action; stop if exit or controller availability is uncertain.

Treat the returned RID as a volatile handle and verify the stable key/body before any delete. Add/delete may reassign other IDs, so reconcile canonical content rather than demanding a misleading raw hash equality.

No automatic retry. After ambiguous 24h completion, enumerate once by the unique key instead of re-adding. Delete only a single positively matched RID with a fresh reservation; on mismatch or failed recovery, preserve evidence and escalate without clear/reset.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/variant; BMC/firmware/local-interface identity; official sections 33/43 and Appendix G authority; separate row-1211 OOB identity
Immutable raw/decoded repository export, canonical key/body baseline, repository info/allocation/mode, request-size limit, duplicate scan and downstream monitoring baseline

Approved record source/revision/hash and full decoded header/key/body, Record-ID placeholder authority, length calculation, standard or IANA/OEM ownership, inert/effect oracle and explicit confirmation
Exact 24h request/completion, returned RID, post-add repository info, fresh reservations and complete ordered 23h reconstruction with byte comparison
Expected versus actual sensor/inventory/threshold/alert/control footprint and modal enter/exit audit when applicable

Fresh-reservation identity check, exact 26h delete/returned RID, key absence, canonical repository/count/capacity/overflow reconciliation and explicit PASS/FAIL/NOT READY/N/A; record that the review agent ran no DUT action
test_case.recovery: Precondition execution on targeted Delete 26h and, for modal repositories, Exit 2Bh being authoritative and available. If Add completion is ambiguous, never repeat it: leave modal mode if required, enumerate once by the unique key, and classify zero/one/multiple matches. Delete only the single positively matched record after a fresh reservation and immediate key/body recheck, then reconcile canonical baseline and monitoring. If no unique match, exit fails, delete fails or canonical content diverges, stop all repository writes, preserve exports and alerts, and hand recovery to the BMC/SDR owner. Never clear/repopulate, reset the BMC or automatically retry as an improvised recovery.

source_conflict.reason: The standard resolves 24h request/response, record structure, mode, readback and targeted recovery semantics. The Review layer replaces TBD and log clearing with an approved complete-record fixture and canonical reconciliation; OEM body meaning remains explicitly Project-owned.

blocked.reason: Core Add behavior and a bounded Delete-based recovery are defined. The exact record, target capability, capacity, mode, transport fit and effect oracle are enforceable Project prerequisites, not unresolved protocol semantics.

external_authorities.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1 E7
external_authorities.application: Sections 33.1-33.16 and 43 plus Appendix G define writable/modal repositories, Storage 0Ah/Cmd24h complete-record Add and returned RID, five-byte header/key/body and length rule, reservation cancellation, bounded 23h readback, volatile Record IDs and targeted 26h deletion.

project_authority: The SDR/BMC owner supplies the exact compatible disposable record and placeholder convention, standard/OEM body authority, capability/mode/capacity/transport proof, effect oracle, consumer window, approval and exact delete/exit recovery. The Project cannot invent a generic checksum, guess an OEM payload, accept completion without full readback, substitute Partial Add/OOB, demand impossible raw-hash equality after ID reassignment, or use clear/reset/retry as recovery.
